svg.text: Does grounding in a knowledge graph make guidance better?
Connected Frontiers · 11 generated use-case tasks + 11 object tasks · KB v20261122-0143 · small model Inkling-2-small vs Qwen-397B from memory
Robust: a small model that edits its own draft with the graph beats a 397B model from memory (0.98, also length-matched).
Not yet robust: memory-first vs memory (0.91, but 0.59 when answer length is matched).
P(first answer preferred) · both orders × persona and expert roles · 95% interval · 0.5 = no preference
Share of the question's gold facts · Inkling-2-small · mean over tasks and 3 trials
Asking for objects: models, papers, methods, tools, benchmarks, datasets
Share of gold objects of each type retrieved / named in the answer · Inkling-2-small · all trials
Papers are retrieved every time and named in no answer: the advice format has no reading-list slot.
What the graph changed in the memory draft (real edits)
Memory-first records every change it makes to the model's own answer; the last one is a failure
Generic 'OpenAI or Anthropic API' replaced with Claude 3.7 Sonnet, the model ScholarQA is
'MoE is production-proven' softened: only DSO National Laboratories shows an org-level MoE
signal, self-claimed and single-source; no production telemetry exists.
Stated explicitly that no deployment workflow, AI methods, models, or benchmarks for
NBCUniversal are covered; discovery and joint metric definition are now step zero rather
QAT demoted from core to stretch goal: quantization-aware training has no usable coverage,
so treat it as exploratory rather than a guaranteed deliverable.
QAT is well established; the graph just does not cover it. Missing ≠ false is still not fully learned.
Tasks are generated from a use-case catalogue (persona + anchor + question + gold facts computed
from the graph), curated and rewritten by a separate model family, leak-checked. Each condition is
scored at three stages against the gold, plus judge preferences in both orders.
Caveats: judges are LLMs (GLM, Nemotron), not people; one trial judged per task; small task sets; answers from the graph are only as good as its mostly self-claimed edges.
